nodes.question: Why is this case study considered relevant?
nodes.answer: It provides a holistic insight into a biologically rich context subjected to severe anthropogenic pressures and involves a mixed semi-industrial fishery.
nodes.paragraph: 2019; FISH4ACP 2021; Penca et al. 2021; Acosta-Alba et al. 2022; Seung 2022). While both perspectives, the ecosystem-based fisheries analysis and the seafood value chain analysis, individually provide interesting results, their optimal potential may be achieved when they are integrated, so environmental fac - tors and human pressures, and the effects of past and future change scenarios can be jointly analysed and predicted. However, due to the technical difficulties and the extended data requirements, there are only a few examples where this integration has been implemented. Up to date, these exam- ples are mostly focused on monospecific fisheries (Khan 2009; Christensen et al. 2011). In this paper, we develop an integrated food web and value chain model of an area of the Northwestern Mediter - ranean Sea. This is a relevant case study, because it provides a holistic insight into a biologically rich context subjected to severe anthropogenic pressures and where a mixed semi- industrial fishery takes place.
